study.question: Does bounded, exchange-invariant restoration of the five-summary amplitude recover part of the terminal-pair symmetric averaging loss under matched retraining, without restoring supplied pair orientation?
study.hypothesis: Observation: supplied terminal-pair summaries score0.66843213, their deterministic mean0.66775417, content-canonical representative0.66717047, and invertible reversal0.66652417, all32192421 parameters at the same seed. Reversal retains orientation information yet hurts more than symmetrization; compressed-feature geometry and frozen-recipe optimization therefore remain consequential alternatives to pure information loss. Symmetric averaging may suppress useful summary amplitude. Multiply the entire concatenated symmetric summary by one pair-exchange-invariant bounded RMS-energy factor. If amplitude suppression explains part of the gap, this representation should recover click AUC while remaining invariant to this pair exchange in its summary path. This is a single-seed scale diagnostic, not a general test of order necessity.

study.proposed_difference: Let x,y concatenate the five summary views before and after exchanging the two greatest-index full blocks, m=(x+y)/2. Apply g*m with g=clip(sqrt((mean((x*x+y*y)/2)+1e-12)/(mean(m*m)+1e-12)),1,2). One scalar per row preserves every summary channel direction and their relative amplitudes. Energies are FP32 under low-precision inputs, FP64 for fixtures; the inherited mean is cast before scaling. Gain is differentiated, has no state/parameters/RNG, equals1 for identical views, and is capped2 for cancellation stability. eps and cap are fixed prospectively, not tuned. Only the five-summary path removes terminal-pair orientation; pooling, within-block order, partial-block placement and other inherited information remain.
predictions: The actual operator must be exchange invariant in values and transported gradients, finite for exact/near cancellation and low precision, identity for equal views, and nontrivially rescale nondegenerate fixtures. Full-model parameter/state shapes and initialization must match the ancestor.

If a valid, effective rescaling does not improve over0.6677541749411481, this bounded scale-restoration implementation does not explain/recover the symmetric deficit under this recipe. It does not refute useful order, all scale treatments or all invariant replacements.

AUC below the predeclared partial-recovery threshold fails the stronger partial-recovery prediction. AUC improvement alone does not confirm amplitude as the cause because the orbit-energy scalar also supplies invariant content and changes gradients.
A material cost increase without quality recovery rejects this candidate as an efficiency improvement.
alternative_explanations: Supplied order may carry useful signal beyond exchange-invariant features; the intervention still discards antisymmetric directions.

The orbit-energy scalar is additional invariant content relative to the mean, so a benefit may reflect restored heterogeneity information, input conditioning or regularization rather than amplitude alone.
Differentiating the scale changes item-embedding gradients. Numerical rounding, clipping saturation, shared embeddings, surrogate auxiliary transfer and the frozen one-pass optimizer can interact.
Existing trials use a single paired seed. Exact same-seed identity bridges are reproducibility, not independent repetitions; seed variation and user clustering remain unresolved.
Two-block summary invariance is conditional and does not establish global history-order invariance. Supplied positions do not expose timestamps or elapsed time.
